scope: American Labor Party research cross-lead: four missing New Kensington labor-dispute defendants, including Progressive Party organizer Harry Truitt. Angola 3 roster also checked.

court.label: Commonwealth v. Truitt, 369 Pa. 72, Pennsylvania Supreme Court, December 19, 1951; majority and Stern concurrence

background.label: William A. Reuben, The Truitt Case, National Guardian, February 27, 1952, p.4 (includes labeled portrait)

custody.label: William A. Reuben, 2nd Truitt trial in Penna. set for March 17, National Guardian, March 5, 1952, p.8

retrial.label: William A. Reuben, 2nd Truitt trial in Pennsylvania ends in acquittal for one, suspended 10 month sentences for 3, National Guardian, March 26, 1952, p.4

prisoner.name: Harry W. Truitt Jr.
prisoner.description: Harry W. Truitt Jr. was a New Kensington dental technician and Progressive Party organizer who supported clothing-store pickets. He served ten months in the resulting prosecution. His conviction was overturned, but a March 1952 retrial ended in a suspended sentence.

cases.charges: Obstructing an officer; assault and battery; aggravated assault and battery
cases.sentence: One year plus three years originally imposed. Reversed December 19, 1951. Ten months actually served. Convicted again in March 1952; ten-month sentence suspended.

entries.custody_evidence: March 5 reporting documents ten months already served by all four appellants; March 26 confirms the retrial outcomes.
entries.research_notes: See shared research notes and batch audit. Exact custody endpoints and vital dates remain unverified.

prisoner.name: John F. Allen
prisoner.description: John F. Allen worked in Harry Truitt’s dental laboratory. Arrested during the 1950 New Kensington picketing dispute, he served ten months before winning an appeal. A retrial in March 1952 acquitted him.

cases.charges: Obstructing an officer; assault and battery; aggravated assault and battery
cases.sentence: One year plus three years originally imposed. Reversed December 19, 1951. Ten months actually served. Acquitted at the March 1952 retrial.

entries.custody_evidence: March 5 reporting documents ten months already served by all four appellants; March 26 confirms the retrial outcomes.
entries.research_notes: See shared research notes and batch audit. Exact custody endpoints and vital dates remain unverified.

prisoner.name: Lester Peay
prisoner.description: Lester Peay was a picket in the 1950 New Kensington clothing-store dispute. He served ten months in the resulting prosecution. After his conviction was overturned, a March 1952 retrial ended in a suspended sentence.

cases.charges: Obstructing an officer; assault and battery; aggravated assault and battery

prisoner.name: Robert T. Smith
prisoner.description: Robert T. Smith led clothing-store pickets in New Kensington in 1950. He served ten months following an affray conviction. After a successful appeal, a March 1952 retrial ended in a suspended sentence.

cases.sentence: 18 months to three years originally imposed. Reversed December 19, 1951. Ten months actually served. Convicted again in March 1952; ten-month sentence suspended.

research_notes: The court identifies Truitt, Allen, Peay and Smith as appellants. Do not substitute Tarpley, whose sentence was deferred, or initial arrestee Kuchek. The newspaper calls the jail Westmoreland County workhouse; the court names Allegheny County Workhouse as the sentencing destination. Facility relation left unset pending reconciliation. No continuous arrest-to-release interval is established. The documented ten months predates the retrial and is not calculated from its suspended sentence. Newspaper freed wording is not an exact physical-release date. No blanket acquittal or proven frame-up claim. Coordinates approximate New Kensington, not a jail entrance. Smith is a different person from the existing Beale anti-drone protester Robert Smith. No formal union membership is asserted for the pickets or laboratory assistant; the court distinguishes paid picketing from Local 65 membership. Exact vital dates and three other portraits not verified; age estimates and unrelated namesakes excluded.
